summary: The milestone completed 13 experiments in 5.8 minutes, including 7 compute-bound experiments. The 3.75-minute readiness-gated canonical factor transport canary and the 1.72-minute canonical factor-edit contract led the compute tail. The locked task classification found no GPU-idle fault on compute-bound work, and the supplied data does not establish parallel model loading or runner selection.
bottlenecks_identified: The Exp6379-readiness-gated canonical factor transport canary was the longest compute-bound entry at 3.75 minutes. Its label identifies readiness gating, but the supplied timing data has no phase breakdown for a finer cause.
The canonical factor-edit instruction and capacity transport contract was the next-longest compute-bound entry at 1.72 minutes. The supplied timing data does not identify why it took that long.
Disk-mtime reconstruction ranks the work but does not separate readiness wait, setup, inference, and teardown time.
improvements_suggested: Add a readiness-aware preflight before scheduling gated compute work, and record gate-wait and compute-phase timestamps.
Attach GPU utilization samples to the active task and phase so a task-untied idle snapshot cannot be mistaken for in-task utilization.
Record model-count and runner-dispatch receipts for every compute task. Require DualGPURunner only when at least two models load in parallel.
Schedule independent synthesis work while a compute task waits on readiness.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Add readiness preflight and separate gate-wait timing for gated compute tasks.
Capture task-linked GPU utilization from compute start through compute end.
Emit model-count and runner-dispatch receipts, with DualGPURunner selected only for parallel multi-model work.
meta_reflection: The reconstructed timing can rank experiments, but it cannot distinguish gate wait from active compute. The savings estimate remains 0 because the supplied evidence contains no measured counterfactual; better task-linked telemetry should make the next estimate evidence-based.
